places.name: Aberdeen Maritime Museum
places.ai_summary: A fascinating museum showcasing Aberdeen’s maritime history, including exhibits on shipbuilding, fishing, and the North Sea oil industry.

opening_hours.notes: Closed on major public holidays.

places.place_tip: Don’t miss the view of the harbor from the museum’s upper floors.

places.ai_summary: A beautiful park featuring a wide variety of plants, trees, and flowers, as well as a large pond and play areas for children.

opening_hours.notes: Winter Gardens open daily from 10:00 AM - 4:00 PM.

places.place_tip: Check out the Victorian bandstand and the various themed gardens.

opening_hours.notes: Access to some buildings may be restricted during university holidays.

places.place_tip: Visit the King’s College Chapel and the nearby St. Machar’s Cathedral.

places.place_tip: Attend a service or concert for a truly memorable experience.

places.place_tip: Enjoy a walk along the beach and take in the views of the North Sea.

places.name: Aberdeen Art Gallery
places.ai_summary: An impressive art gallery housing an extensive collection of paintings, sculptures, and decorative arts, with a focus on Scottish artists.

opening_hours.notes: Closed on major public holidays.

places.place_tip: Check out the gallery shop for unique art-inspired gifts.

places.name: Union Street
places.ai_summary: The main shopping street in Aberdeen, featuring a wide range of shops, cafes, and restaurants, as well as impressive granite architecture.

opening_hours.notes: Individual shop hours may vary.

places.place_tip: Look out for the various street performers and events that take place throughout the year.

places.name: Provost Skene’s House
places.ai_summary: A historic house museum displaying the life and times of a wealthy Aberdeen family in the 17th century, with period furnishings and exhibits.

opening_hours.notes: Closed on major public holidays.

places.place_tip: Join one of the guided tours for a more in-depth understanding of the house’s history.

places.name: The Tolbooth Museum
places.ai_summary: A small museum located in a historic building that was once a jail and town hall, featuring exhibits on Aberdeen’s history and heritage.

opening_hours.notes: Closed on major public holidays.

places.place_tip: Check out the museum shop for unique souvenirs and local crafts.

places.name: Aberdeen Beach Esplanade
places.ai_summary: A long sandy beach with a wide esplanade, popular for walking, cycling, and picnicking, with stunning views of the North Sea.

opening_hours.notes: Parking charges apply in nearby car parks.

places.place_tip: Visit the beach at sunset for a truly magical experience.

places.name: Seaton Park
places.ai_summary: A large public park with beautiful gardens, woodlands, and a pond, offering a peaceful retreat from the city.

opening_hours.notes: Park gates are locked at night.

places.place_tip: Bring a picnic and enjoy a relaxing day in the park.

places.ai_summary: A lovely botanic garden with a wide variety of plants, trees, and flowers, as well as a glasshouse and rock garden.

opening_hours.notes: Closed on major public holidays.

places.place_tip: Join one of the guided tours to learn more about the plants and gardens.

attribution.title: Huntly station geograph-3537622-by-Ben-Brooksbank
attribution.author: Ben Brooksbank
attribution.description:
Huntly station, 1997.
View northward, towards Keith, then Elgin and Inverness by the ex-Highland Railway route. This station is on the surviving section of the ex-GNSR main line from Aberdeen, which used to go until 1968 to Elgin also via Cairnie Junction and Buckie.

places.name: Dunnottar Castle (Stonehaven)

opening_hours.notes: Last admission 1 hour before closing. Closed on major public holidays.

places.place_tip: Wear comfortable shoes for exploring the castle and surrounding trails.
